claims.head: A shadow job for Protas, Jenner and Wilson
claims.call: The Capitals’ L2 (Protas, Jenner and Wilson) spends at least 43% of its 5-on-5 time against the Kings’ first line, against about 30% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Capitals keep sending Wilson’s line (Protas, Jenner and Wilson) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Spencer Carbery has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Kings’ first line is Panarin, Byfield and Kempe.

notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 4 of their last 6 games, including the last one. Erik Haula takes shifts on two lines, L2 and L3. Brian Dumoulin is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Anderson and Ceci.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 8 games cover only 27% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Jakob Chychrun has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, up from 8% last season.

stakes: The Kings go in eighth in the Pacific with 2 points, the Capitals third in the Metropolitan with 10 points.

WSH.head: A slightly uphill night for the Capitals
WSH.body: Even though Washington has home-ice advantage, Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Capitals’ best way to tip it is keeping dangerous shots away.

LAK.head: The Kings have a slight edge
LAK.body: Even though Washington has home-ice advantage, Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. Still, it’s close: the Capitals can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

story.head: Still no win for the Kings
paras: The Kings are still looking for their first win of the season, 0-4-2 through six games. The Capitals have won two in a row.

It’s strength against strength: the Capitals are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Kings are the best at preventing dangerous shots. At home, Spencer Carbery likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Kings’ first line.

items.text: Alex Tuch has six goals in six games against Los Angeles since 2023-24, most of them with Buffalo.
The Kings have been without Alex Turcotte since Oct 6, and have had to make do without Kevin Fiala all season.
The Capitals have been without Pierre-Luc Dubois and Rasmus Sandin for several games.
Mats Zuccarello has missed the Kings’ last three games.
